land.text: the Balearic Islands, Dénia's since 1015 and autonomous under the governor Abd Allah ibn Aglab from 1050

predecessors.note: Cliopatria keeps the islands inside its Taifa of Dénia shapes to 1125 (bbox to 4.3 E).

land.text: the Balearic Islands, where the Almohads 'installed their own governors' after executing Abdallah ibn Ishaq in 1203

successors.note: Crown of Aragon conquers Majorca on 31 December 1229 (not on the pages opened here).

capitals.name: Madīna Mayūrqa (Palma de Mallorca)
capitals.note: Not named on the Taifa page; the expedition page has the Crusaders invest Palma de Majorca in August 1114 and the city capitulate in April 1115. Held only in the two periods the ledger gives.

rulers.name: Mubassir
rulers.note: The Taifa page's spelling; the expedition page does not name him.

rulers.name: Abu-l-Rabi Sulayman 'El Burabe'
rulers.note: The Taifa page lists him 1114-1126; the expedition page's infobox has him as the prisoner taken to Pisa in 1115, so only 1114-1115 is the taifa's.

rulers.name: Muhammad I ibn Ali ibn Yusuf (Banu Ghaniya)
rulers.note: Appointed Almoravid governor of the Balearic Islands in 1126 (Banu Ghaniya page); independent after the Almoravids fell (1147); the Banu Ghaniya page has him replaced by his son in a palace coup in 1156.

rulers.name: Ishaq
rulers.note: Died on a pirate expedition in 1183 (Banu Ghaniya page); the Taifa page lists him to 1184.

rulers.name: Muhammad ibn Ishaq (Muhammad II)
rulers.note: Submitted to the Almohads and was overthrown in 1184.

rulers.name: Ali ibn Ishaq
rulers.note: Left for the eastern Maghreb in 1184; the Almohads retook the islands in 1185.

rulers.name: Abdallah ibn Ishaq
rulers.note: Recaptured the islands from the Almohads by 1187; defeated and executed by them in 1203.

correction.text: the Balearic Islands as one taifa, 'the first taifa lasted for about 50 years (1076-1116)'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has no row; its Taifa of Dénia shapes (1040-1125, 20.7-21.0 thousand km2, bbox to 4.30 E) carry the islands and must lose them. The pages never list the islands (Majorca, Ibiza, Menorca, Formentera); the Balearic Islands region is the reading. No infobox area. The Christian occupation of 1114-1115 is in the ledger.

correction.text: the Balearic Islands under the Banu Ghaniya, 'a new, independent kingdom' (the second taifa, 1147-1203)
the Balearic Islands recaptured by Abdallah ibn Ishaq 'by 1187'; 1185-1186 they were Almohad

keyframe_review.note: Third period; the Almohads installed governors only after 1203.

ledger.note: 1076: the Balearic Islands become the independent Taifa of Majorca under Ibn Aglab al-Murtada. 'The first taifa lasted for about 50 years (1076-1116).' The infobox span of the page is 1018-1203 and credits Mujahid al-Amiri of Dénia as founder; the ruler table runs Mujahid 1018-1041, Ali Iqbal ud-Dawla 1041-1075, Ibn Aglab 1076-1093. The islands are Dénia's client from 1050 in the Dénia dossier.

August 1114: the Pisan-Catalan fleet holds Ibiza and invests Palma. 'The Crusaders invested Palma de Majorca in August 1114'; a fleet of eighty ships arrived from Pisa in spring 1114 and raided Ibiza in June. Ramon Berenguer III of Barcelona (county-of-barcelona) signed the 1113 treaty and took part.

1115: 'In 1115 they were reconquered by the Almoravids of peninsular Iberia.' The Taifa page ends the first taifa in 1116 and says it 'fell to a Christian crusade' and was 'later occupied by the Almoravids'. Banu Ghaniya governors (Muhammad from 1126) ruled for the Almoravids until 1147.
April 1115: 'the city capitulated and its entire population was enslaved'; the Crusaders left within months and the taifa ruler was taken to Pisa.

region.text: the Balearic Islands under Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Ghaniya

ledger.note: 1147: after the Almoravids fall at Marrakesh the islands become independent: 'A new, independent kingdom arose, the second taifa (1147-1203), under the Banu Ghaniya dynasty.' The Banu Ghaniya page: the dynasty kept the islands and 'repelled several Almohad attacks'; Muhammad became independent after his brother Yahya died c. 1148-1149.

1185: 'In his absence, the Almohads retook the islands in 1185' while Ali ibn Ishaq was campaigning in the eastern Maghreb; Muhammad ibn Ishaq was reinstalled under Almohad suzerainty. The Almoravid and Almohad dossiers book this event with almoravid-dynasty as the other side.

region.text: the Balearic Islands recaptured by Abdallah ibn Ishaq

ledger.note: By 1187: Abdallah ibn Ishaq 'recaptured the islands from the Almohads by 1187'; the page gives no year or method, so the year is the latest it allows.
1203: Abdallah is 'defeated and executed by the Almohads in 1203, who installed their own governors on the islands after this'.

region.text: the Balearic Islands, passed to the Almohads

ledger.note: 1203: the Taifa of Majorca ends; 'Almohads: 1203-1229' in the succession list, then the Crown of Aragon.

wars.name: 1113-1115 Balearic Islands expedition
wars.outcome: A Christian victory: the city of Majorca capitulated in April 1115, but the Crusaders held the islands only a few months and the Almoravids reconquered them in 1115.
wars.note: Treaty of Sant Feliu de Guixols between Pisa and Ramon Berenguer III on 7 September 1113; the page's body dates the expedition 1114-1115.

wars.name: Almohad reconquests of the Balearic Islands
wars.outcome: The Almohads retook the islands in 1185, lost them again by 1187 to Abdallah ibn Ishaq and took them for good in 1203.

certainty.note: The coast bounds the realm, but the pages never say which islands were held (Menorca, Ibiza and Formentera are not named on the Taifa or Banu Ghaniya pages); the Balearic Islands region is the reading. The 1115-1146 and 1185-1186 gaps are other states' rule.

sources.title: Taifa of Mallorca
sources.note: Identity, 1018-1203 span, first taifa 1076-1116, second taifa 1147-1203 under the Banu Ghaniya, ruler table, Almohads 1203-1229; no territory, capital or area.

sources.title: Banu Ghaniya
sources.note: Muhammad governor 1126, independence, Ishaq, 1183-1187, Almohad retaking 1185, Abdallah executed 1203; no infobox.

sources.title: 1113-1115 Balearic Islands expedition
sources.note: Pisan-Catalan expedition: treaty 7 Sept 1113, Ibiza June 1114, Palma invested Aug 1114, capitulation April 1115, Almoravids from 1115. The title page Balearic_Islands_expedition is a disambiguation page and was not used.

notes: Written for eu-12-x (requested by eu-12-e as taifa-of-majorca); three pages. Cliopatria has no row for the Balearic taifa: the islands sit inside its Taifa of Dénia shapes to 1125. The Taifa page dates the taifa 1018-1203 in its infobox, but its text gives two periods (1076-1116 and 1147-1203); the dossier takes 1076 as the start because the Dénia dossier books the islands as Dénia's client 1050-1076 and the page's ruler table credits Mujahid, Ali Iqbal and Ibn Aglab. The years 1115-1146 are Almoravid rule (Muhammad ibn Ali as governor from 1126). Conflicts: the Almoravid and Almohad dossiers count the Banu Ghaniya's Balearics as Almoravid land throughout (1115, 1185, 1187, 1203 events with almoravid-dynasty / almohad-caliphate as counterpart); this dossier books 1147-1185 and 1187-1203 as independent per the Taifa page, so a reconciler should have the Almoravid dossier cede the islands in 1147. Disagreement: Abu-l-Rabi Sulayman listed 1114-1126 on the Taifa page but the prisoner of the 1115 capture on the expedition page. Not settled: Ali ibn Ishaq and his successors' campaigns in the Maghreb (Bougie, Constantine, Algiers, 1184-1237/38) are the Banu Ghaniya's wider state, not this one; they need an Africa-group dossier (banu-ghaniya) if wanted. The Crown of Aragon dossier books the 1229 conquest from almohad-caliphate. Gazetteer: the Balearic Islands region exists; nothing else is used.
